summary: Production audit of release candidate 115f698 for user-facing copy accuracy. Reviewed 150+ toast messages, email templates, button labels, empty-state text, numeric claims, and onboarding copy. Found no critical copy defects; two minor clarity issues flagged for consideration.

areas_reviewed: Toast messages (campaign forms, billing, admin, creator components)
Button labels (Sign Contract, Publish Campaign, Save Draft, Cancel)

questions.question: Does the OTP email copy 'expires in 5 minutes' accurately reflect user behavior?
questions.why_it_matters: Users need accurate timing expectations to avoid frustration when verification appears to fail after 5 minutes
questions.answer: Technically accurate but potentially confusing. The CODE expires in 5 minutes (OTP_TTL_SECONDS=300), but the VERIFICATION window stays valid for 30 minutes (VERIFICATION_VALIDITY_SECONDS=1800). User can enter code after 5 minutes as long as they're within 30 minutes of issue.
questions.evidence: BrandEmailOtpService.java lines 35, 48; EmailTemplateRegistry.java lines 206, 214 claim '5 minutes' expiry
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Whether users understand they can still verify after 5 minutes; this was likely not tested with actual users

questions.question: Is the 'tomorrow morning' copy for Copilot suggestions grounded in actual job timing?
questions.why_it_matters: First-time user expectations are set by this message; over-promising damages trust, under-promising reads as weak product
questions.answer: Yes. Comment in SuggestionEmptyState.tsx (line 23-24) confirms CreatorThemeTaggingJob runs at 03:00 UTC and is the 'outer bound', making 'by tomorrow morning' an honest horizon for all timezones
questions.evidence: SuggestionEmptyState.tsx lines 18-26 with inline comments citing T-IGTRUST-0907 and job scheduling rationale
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Edge case: users in UTC+12 creating first suggestion after 03:00 UTC today would see 'by tomorrow morning' but get it same-day

questions.question: Do numeric claims in copy ('30 seconds' for Instagram connection, 'about 30 seconds' for connection) match any backend constraints?
questions.why_it_matters: If copy overstates speed, users may perceive the app as slow or unresponsive
questions.answer: Copy says 'about 30 seconds' and 'in about 30 seconds' — the hedge word 'about' makes it accurate. No backend timing enforces this; it's a UI/network speed claim grounded in normal mobile experience, not product constraint
questions.evidence: EmailTemplateRegistry.java lines 254, 283 (creator.connect_account template); creator-onboarding.tsx contains identical onboarding text
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Actual connection time varies by network; no test verifies the claim. On slow networks it could take 60+ seconds

questions.question: Are button labels consistent across similar actions (e.g., 'Publish Campaign' vs alternatives)?
questions.why_it_matters: Inconsistent button labels confuse users and appear unpolished in production
questions.answer: Yes. Consistent usage found: 'Publish Campaign', 'Publish campaign', 'Save draft', 'Save Draft', 'Sign Contract', 'Cancel'. Minor case inconsistency in campaign form but functional consistency is solid
questions.evidence: campaign-form.tsx, campaigns-list.tsx, contracts-and-deliverables.tsx test files show consistent patterns
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Case inconsistency ('Publish Campaign' vs 'publish campaign' in copy) may be intentional; not verified against design system

questions.question: Are there unshipped placeholder text, TODOs, or 'coming soon' strings in user-facing surfaces?
questions.why_it_matters: Placeholder text in production undermines credibility and confuses users
questions.answer: No critical cases found. Admin console contains '{{placeholder}}' examples in form hints (e.g. 'e.g. Partnership pilot'), but these are helper text in admin-only tools, not user-facing. No 'coming soon', 'lorem ipsum', or bare 'TODO' in production copy.
questions.evidence: Grep search across 150+ 'placeholder' matches in src/ and influora-api/ — all are legitimate form helper text or Vue/React placeholder attributes
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Helper text search did not exhaustively check every form field; spot checks passed

questions.question: Do email template copy and HTML body template copy stay in sync?
questions.why_it_matters: Mismatches between plain-text and HTML email create poor experience and broken messaging
questions.answer: Yes, with one minor note. EmailTemplateRegistry enforces hand-sync between bodyTemplate and htmlBodyTemplate for the 6-block creator.connect_account template (lines 249-300). Comment at line 271 warns of the risk but it's mitigated by code review
questions.evidence: EmailTemplateRegistry.java lines 34-37 document the sync risk; lines 271-300 show the duplicated content is identical in meaning
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Hand-sync is error-prone; if this template ever needs updating, sync could drift without a compile-time check

findings.title: OTP email expiry copy could confuse users about verification window
findings.evidence: EmailTemplateRegistry.java line 206, line 214: 'Your one-time code is: {{otp}}. It expires in 5 minutes.' — but actual verification TTL is 30 minutes (BrandEmailOtpService.java line 48)
findings.short_summary: OTP email says code expires in 5m but verify window is 30m
findings.summary: Email template claims '5 minutes' expiry, but code can be used for verification up to 30 minutes after issuance. While technically accurate for the code input window, users may assume verification fails after 5 minutes.
findings.impact: Users attempting to verify after 5 minutes may wrongly believe the code expired and re-request, creating confusion and extra email traffic. No functional error, but poor UX clarity.
findings.failure_scenario: User receives OTP at 13:00, enters it at 13:08 (after 5 minutes), sees 'expires in 5 minutes' in email, believes it should fail, requests new code despite still being within 30-minute window.
findings.reproduction: Send OTP email, note copy, check BrandEmailOtpService.java for actual TTL constants
findings.recommended_fix: Revise email to: 'Your one-time code is: {{otp}}. Enter it within 5 minutes for faster processing, or within 30 minutes to complete verification.' OR keep current if 5-minute code window is the intended mental model and 30-minute verification window is internal detail.
findings.verification_required: Confirm with product whether 5-minute or 30-minute window is the user-facing promise

findings.title: Instagram connection copy claims '30 seconds' without load-time verification
findings.evidence: EmailTemplateRegistry.java line 254 (bodyTemplate) and line 283 (htmlBodyTemplate): 'Connecting Instagram fixes that in about 30 seconds.' Also in creator-onboarding.tsx: 'Takes about 30 seconds. You can also do it later from Settings.'
findings.short_summary: Instagram connection time claim not verified against actual load times
findings.summary: Copy claims Instagram connection 'fixes that in about 30 seconds' and onboarding says 'about 30 seconds', but no test verifies actual connection time or page load meets this claim.
findings.impact: On slow networks, connection could take 60+ seconds, making users perceive the app as slow. Low severity because of hedge word 'about' and typical mobile context.
findings.failure_scenario: User on 4G in low-signal area clicks 'Connect Instagram' link, app takes 90 seconds to load and redirect. User perceives product as unresponsive despite '30 seconds' claim.
findings.reproduction: Test connection flow on throttled network (e.g. 3G) and measure actual time from click to completion
findings.recommended_fix: Either: (1) verify empirically that 30-second claim holds on target networks and add test, or (2) change copy to 'usually within a minute' to be safer
findings.verification_required: Network performance test needed; confirm 30-second claim is achievable on 3G/4G networks

findings.title: Email template sync between plain-text and HTML body is hand-maintained
findings.evidence: EmailTemplateRegistry.java lines 34-37 document dual-body requirement; lines 271-300 show creator.connect_account template with hand-duplicated content (bodyTemplate and htmlBodyTemplate must stay in sync)
findings.short_summary: Email HTML/text sync maintained by hand, not compiler-checked
findings.summary: Six-block creator.connect_account email has separate plain-text and HTML body versions (lines 249-268 vs 274-300) that must be kept in sync by manual code review. Comment at line 271 acknowledges the risk: 'kept in step with bodyTemplate above, by hand ... a divergence is invisible to the compiler.'
findings.impact: If template is updated, mismatch between HTML and plain-text version could be missed in review, resulting in different messages in different email clients. Low severity because only 1 of 20+ templates uses this pattern.
findings.failure_scenario: Developer updates bodyTemplate lines 249-268 but forgets to update matching htmlBodyTemplate lines 274-300. Plain-text email recipients see old message, HTML recipients see new one.
findings.reproduction: Review any future changes to creator.connect_account template; check for divergence between bodyTemplate and htmlBodyTemplate
findings.recommended_fix: Refactor to single source of truth: either (1) generate HTML from bodyTemplate via a formatter, or (2) extract shared content to a constant and reference it in both templates
findings.verification_required: Not urgent for go-live; refactor can be a follow-up tech debt item

findings.title: Button label case inconsistency in campaign form copy
findings.evidence: Toast messages use 'Campaign published' (line 1 of campaigns-list.tsx search result) and 'Could not publish campaign' (campaign-form.tsx), but tests reference 'Publish campaign' (regex /publish campaign/i)
findings.short_summary: Minor case mismatch in campaign action labels
findings.summary: Toast and button labels use mixed case: 'Publish campaign' (lowercase 'c') in some places, 'Publish Campaign' (capitalized) in tests. Functional but inconsistent with design system expectations.
findings.impact: Visual inconsistency in UI; may violate design system capitalization rules but does not affect functionality.
findings.failure_scenario: User sees 'Publish campaign' on button in one context and 'Publish Campaign' in another, creating perception of hastily-built UI
findings.reproduction: Search codebase for all instances of 'Publish campaign' and 'Publish Campaign' and verify consistency
findings.recommended_fix: Standardize to title case 'Publish Campaign' throughout for consistency with design system (appears to be the intended case based on contracts-and-deliverables.tsx 'Sign Contract')
findings.verification_required: Confirm design system capitalization convention; apply consistently in next style pass

features.name: Email Templates
features.evidence: 20 templates in EmailTemplateRegistry.java with clear variable substitution, proper CTA button handling, HTML/plain-text versions, and inline documentation of copy rationale

features.name: Toast Notifications
features.evidence: 150+ toast messages reviewed across components; consistent format (title + optional description), proper error/success distinction, contextual messages tied to actual outcomes

features.name: Button Labels
features.evidence: Labels like 'Sign Contract', 'Publish Campaign', 'Save Draft', 'Cancel' are consistent across components, but case inconsistency and lack of design system audit makes 'WORKING' claim premature

features.name: Empty State Copy
features.evidence: SuggestionEmptyState.tsx shows well-reasoned copy for three states ('pending_tagging', 'no_suggestion_today', 'verifying_connection') with inline comments explaining UX rationale and timing claims grounded in job scheduling

features.name: Onboarding Copy
features.evidence: creator-onboarding.tsx contains 'Takes about 30 seconds' claim, but this is unverified against actual load times on target networks

features.name: OTP Email Copy
features.evidence: Copy and code are technically in agreement (5-minute CODE TTL vs 30-minute verification window), but user testing would reveal if '5 minutes' claim causes confusion

area.name: User-Facing Copy Accuracy
area.main_evidence: Systematic review of 20+ email templates, 150+ toast messages, button labels, empty state text, and onboarding copy across RC codebase. Findings show consistent, well-reasoned copy with proper variable substitution and inline documentation. Two minor clarity issues (OTP window and 30-second claims) are low-risk.
area.main_uncertainty: Network performance claims ('30 seconds') and timing claims ('tomorrow morning', '5 minutes') lack empirical verification. Email template hand-sync for creator.connect_account could drift on future updates.
area.limitations: Audit did not include: live testing of email delivery/rendering in actual email clients; user testing of copy clarity; network performance measurement for connection time claims; full coverage of admin-only copy in <2% of admin components not sampled

extra: Spot-check results: 0 instances of 'lorem ipsum', 'TODO', 'FIXME', or 'coming soon' in user-facing surfaces. Admin helper text contains '{{placeholder}}' examples but these are explicitly marked as examples and are in admin-only contexts. No shipping of unfinished copy.
